findings.where: explain, paragraph 4 (and whatAmILookingAt's motor and pump part)
findings.what: The lesson says the gap between the motor and pump curves shrinks as the shaft speeds up, so the speed climbs more and more slowly. The rig's own curves on screen 11 show something else: the gap widens from 130 N m at rest to about 232 N m near 1125 rev/min before it closes, and the speed trace curves upward before it bends over. Say the gap widens while the motor nears its peak, then closes fast near full speed.

findings.where: screens 3 and 7 (push and work pictures, T3 and T7)
findings.what: The push equals the torque ÷ r only on a shaft with one arm. Screens 3 and 7 show 'T = 50 N m, push 250 N' and say 'Follow one mass' straight after the two-mass rig at 50 N m. On that rig each arm takes half the torque, a 125 N push at 0.2 m, and 250 N on 25 kg would give 50 rad/s², not the 25 rad/s² screen 1 showed. Say 'Picture a shaft with just one arm', as the explain does, or halve the push for each arm.

The lead line repeats the screen's first sentence: a motor turning a shaft with two arms, each carrying a 25 kg mass. So Dan reads about 112 words before the picture, which is over the 90-word limit. Drop T1's first sentence, or move the lead's 'these are examples' note into the caption.

findings.where: live sentence under the steady-torque runs (screens 1, 5, 9, 11)
findings.what: The time is rounded to 0.1 s but the speed is worked out from the unrounded time, so the sentence does not check by hand. 'After 0.7 s the shaft turns at 16.7 rad/s. It gains 25 rad/s every second' gives 17.5, not 16.7. 'After 1.9 s … 24.4 rad/s … 13.06' gives 24.8. Work the speed out from the time as shown.

'So the speed line climbs steeply, then bends over' does not match the drawn S-shaped trace. The trace starts gently and gets steeper as the gap widens, then bends over. Say it climbs faster and faster at first, then bends over.

findings.where: screen 11, torque against speed graph at 360 px
findings.what: The x-axis tick labels '1000' and '1500' nearly touch. Drop one label or space the ticks.
The '72.4 N m' label sits mid-shaft between the motor's arrow and the pump's arrow, so it is not clear which torque it names. Put it by the motor's arrow, for example 'motor 72.4 N m'.

findings.where: screen 5, end sentence after dragging the right rig inside 0.2 m
findings.what: The sentence reads '0.25 times as long: 1.5 s against 6.1 s'. Say 'a quarter as long'.

The brief promised that a flywheel uses its ½Iω² store to smooth an engine's uneven torque, as on a diesel generator. The lesson leaves it out, and it is the one tie to the diesel generator backup Dan works with. One sentence would do it.

'It is just like a trolley rolling at a steady speed' comes before the thing it compares, so 'It' has nothing clear to point at. Lead with 'A shaft turning at a steady speed has no net torque on it', then give the trolley comparison.
The footnote sits on the basic definition 'the turning effect of a force', which Dan would never look up on a job. Drop it and keep [^2], the rule to convert to rad/s.
